title: Final: exceptions and reliability
sub: Two passes, rethrowing, broken types and cost
cards/0/q: Log prints a string and returns true only for "B". What does the program print?
cards/0/explain: First pass: filter A is false, the search goes on, filter B is true. Only now does the second pass unwind the stack: the inner finally prints F. The catch body runs last.
cards/0/wrong/1: The inner try's finally runs in the second pass, which starts only after the first pass has found a handler — filter B.
cards/1/q: In which cases will finally not run? Select all.
cards/1/options/1: The try is left by a break out of a loop
cards/1/options/2: The process is killed with SIGKILL
cards/1/options/3: The exception is caught in the calling method
cards/1/explain: Environment.Exit inside try does not run that thread's finally, and SIGKILL lets the process run nothing at all. break and an exception caught higher up are normal exits.
cards/2/q: The LIMIT variable is not set. Accessing Settings.Path throws TypeInitializationException. Which line is the real cause?
cards/2/explain: int.Parse(null) throws ArgumentNullException, which ends up in InnerException. The initializers of all fields form one static constructor, so the whole type is broken, Path included, until the process restarts.
cards/3/q: A background thread saved a caught exception in a field. The main thread must throw it with the original stack. How?
cards/3/options/0: ExceptionDispatchInfo.Capture(e) in the thread, Throw() in the main one
cards/3/options/1: throw saved; in the main thread
cards/3/explain: ExceptionDispatchInfo throws the same object and keeps the original stack, appending the new frames after a separator. await works the same way.
cards/3/wrong/1: throw saved starts the stack at this line; the place in the background thread is lost.
cards/3/wrong/2: throw; without an argument outside a catch is compile error CS0156.
cards/4/q: Match how it was in .NET Framework with how it is now
cards/4/pairs/3/1: Unhandled on any thread crashes the process
cards/5/q: In a hot loop half the keys are missing from the dictionary. What is wrong with this code?
cards/5/options/0: Every miss is a throw with a stack walk and unwind, microseconds instead of nanoseconds; use TryGetValue
cards/5/options/1: Nothing: a try without an exception is free, and an exception costs as much as an if
cards/5/options/2: The dictionary indexer returns default for a missing key, so the catch never fires
cards/5/options/3: KeyNotFoundException must not be caught, it is a runtime exception
cards/5/explain: The try itself costs almost nothing; the throw is what is expensive. When a missing key is an ordinary outcome, check it with a value: TryGetValue does one lookup and does not throw.
cards/5/wrong/2: The Dictionary indexer throws KeyNotFoundException. GetValueOrDefault and TryGetValue are the ones that return default.
cards/6/q: What is true about AppDomain.UnhandledException? Select all.
cards/6/options/0: It fires for an unhandled exception on any thread
cards/6/options/1: It lets you cancel process termination
cards/6/options/2: It is the place to write a log and flush buffers
cards/6/options/3: It fires for an exception in a Task nobody awaited
cards/6/explain: It is a notification before the crash: IsTerminating is true and it cannot be cancelled. Exceptions of unawaited tasks go to TaskScheduler.UnobservedTaskException and do not crash the process.
cards/7/q: The boundary of a background job: log any error, but let cancellation through
cards/7/explain: The when filter excludes OperationCanceledException: cancellation is not caught and stops the work, while the other errors go to the log.
